spec: §8.4 + §6.2 + §6.5 + §14 — restore wire-function vectors: restore->re-announce (counter floor + 1024, next = +1), restore->send (per-peer send-counter resumption), announce sync-commit, unclean-reboot forward jump
description: State-ABSENT restore (words/QR only): the node MUST NOT announce until a counter floor is set; set_restore_floor(F) commits announce_last = F + 1024 and traffic_base = 1024 (fsync, before any announce); the first announce then uses F + 1025 and the first send counter to a new peer is 1025 (the same +1024 jump). Over-jumping is harmless (gaps only advance windows); under-jumping would strand the node at peers permanently. Section 6.2 sync-commit: next_announce_counter() persists the value BEFORE returning it, so after a crash (no shutdown) a reopened store never re-issues a transmitted counter. Section 6.5: after an UNCLEAN reboot both sides apply a forward jump J = batch_n (>= N) to per-peer send counters and receive high-waters AND to traffic_base (so peers first contacted < N ops before the crash, absent from the file, also resume above every uncommitted emission); the announce counter is never jumped. create() and set_restore_floor() persist CLEAN (no emission yet); the first emission marks the file running, so first_send_to_new_peer = 1025 holds after a clean shutdown/reopen. Counters are decimal strings (u64).
provenance: Derived from counters.rs / backup.rs restore semantics and asserted against the live CounterStore at generation time (restore_pending -> set_restore_floor -> next_announce_counter).

restore_edges.name: floor + 1024 == u64::MAX: floor commits, but the first announce overflows (no wrap)

unclean_reboot.note: send side: sends 5 and 6 were emitted but uncommitted; the reopened store jumps by J = batch_n = 4, so the next send (9) can never collide with an emitted counter. receive side (separate store): receives 5 and 6 were consumed but uncommitted; the reopened window high-water jumps from the committed 4 to 8 (J = 4). Batch commits fire every batch_n operations (sends and receives share the tick).
